e-5677.knowledge_point: Calculating the Number of Combinations of Objects Chosen From a Group Fewer Than Ten
e-5677.problem: There are $10$ employees in a company, and $3$ of them are to be selected to form a committee. How many different selections are possible?
e-5677.worked_solution:
The number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_nC_r = \dfrac{n!}{(n-r)!r!}.
$$

There are $10$ employees, so $n=10.$ We want to select $3$ of those employees to form a committee, so we have $r=3.$

Therefore, the number of different ways to form the committee is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{n}{C}_{r} & ={}_{10}{C}_{3} \\  & =\frac{10!}{(10-3)!3!} \\  & =\frac{10!}{7!3!} \\  & =\frac{10\cdot 9\cdot 8\cdot \cancel{7!}}{\cancel{7!}3!} \\  & =\frac{720}{6} \\  & =120.\end{aligned}
$$

e-5676.problem: Suppose a teacher needs to select a group of $4$ students from a class of $20$ students to represent the class in a competition. How many different ways can the teacher form a team of $4$ students?
e-5676.worked_solution:
The number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_nC_r = \dfrac{n!}{(n-r)!r!}.
$$

There are $20$ students, so $n=20.$ We want to select $4$ of those students to form a group, so we have $r=4.$

Therefore, the number of different ways in which the teacher can form the team is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{20}{C}_{4} & =\frac{20!}{(20-4)!4!} \\  & =\frac{20!}{16!4!} \\  & =\frac{20\cdot 19\cdot 18\cdot 17\cdot \cancel{16!}}{\cancel{16!}4!} \\  & =\frac{116\,280}{24} \\  & =4\,845.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$

content.knowledge_point: Evaluating Combinations Given Using Alternate Notation
content.problem: Evaluate $(\frac{5}{1}).$
content.worked_solution:
First, note that $(\frac{5}{1})$ means the same thing as ${}_{5}{C}_{1}.$

 In general, the number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{C}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

Substituting $n=5$ and $r=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{5}{C}_{1} & =\frac{5!}{(5-1)!1!} \\  & =\frac{5!}{4!1!} \\  & =\frac{5\cdot \cancel{4!}}{\cancel{4!}\cdot 1} \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: How many different ways can a group of four be made from a room of eighty people?
after.worked_solution:
In general, the number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{C}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

There are $80$ people, so $n=80.$ We want to select $4$ of those people for each group, so we have $r=4.$

Therefore, the number of different potential groups of four is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{80}{C}_{4} & =\frac{80!}{(80-4)!\,4!} \\  & =\frac{80!}{76!4!} \\  & =\frac{80\cdot 79\cdot 78\cdot 77\cdot \cancel{76!}}{\cancel{76!}4!} \\  & =\frac{80\cdot 79\cdot 78\cdot 77}{4\cdot 3\cdot 2\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{37\,957\,920}{24} \\  & =1\,581\,580.\end{aligned}
$$
